citations.text: Condonation of shortage of attendance to the extent of ten percent (10%), that is, for candidates securing attendance of not less than sixty-five percent (65%) and less than seventy-five percent (75%) in a course, may be granted by the Principal on the recommendation of the Head of the Department, on genuine and verifiable medical grounds, and on payment of the condonation fee prescribed by the College. Application for condonation shall be made in the prescribed form together with supporting medical certification, not later than ten days before the commencement of the semester end examinations.

Condonation under clause 4.5 shall not be granted more than twice during the entire programme, and shall not be granted to a candidate whose attendance in the course concerned is below sixty-five percent (65%) under any circumstances whatsoever.

A minimum attendance of eighty percent (80%) in the pre-placement training programme shall be mandatory. A candidate failing to secure such attendance may be declared ineligible for campus recruitment at the discretion of the Training and Placement Officer.

A candidate shall be required to put in a minimum of seventy-five percent (75%) of attendance in each course, computed on the total number of periods of instruction held in that course during the semester, in order to be eligible to appear for the semester end examination in that course. A candidate who fails to secure the required seventy-five percent (75%) attendance in any course shall be detained in that course and shall not be permitted to appear for the semester end examination therein.
